gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each bank's headline watts leave for the MacBook Air once a phone is also plugged in: the UGREEN "130 W" keeps 100 W on the laptop port (100 + 30), while the Baseus FC41 "100 W" drops to 65 W on one cable with 15 W shared by the rest (Notebookcheck), which is under Apple's 70 W fast-charge line.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's review (cited), Best Batteries' review, MacSources and Parka Blogs, all opened today; us.ugreen.com (cited) and Costco (cited) were not read, the first returning HTTP 429 on every attempt. All four pages opened cover only the UGREEN: Macworld and Best Batteries give its 100 + 30 W split and 115 W three-port total, and Best Batteries, MacSources and Parka Blogs give its 11,000 mAh rated capacity. None sets it beside another 20,000 mAh bank, so none says a bank named "100 W" falls below 70 W when shared, or that three makers' own usable-capacity figures land at 55-60 Wh. The capacity half alone would score 1, because Best Batteries already has it for the UGREEN.
decides: It confirms the UGREEN Nexode 20,000 mAh 130 W as the pick for an Air charged alongside a phone: it is the only one of our two unrecorded 20K candidates whose laptop port stays above Apple's 70 W line when shared. The Baseus FC41 20K 100 W honestly wins the built-in-cable, lightest (428 g), laptop-only segment. Anker Prime (140 W port, 100 W input, $119.99) and Cuktech 15 Ultra (140 W port, 165 W input, 590 g) win on recharge speed, but their extra port power does nothing for an Air. On capacity, the makers' own usable figures (55-60 Wh) say one 13-inch Air charge (53.8 Wh) and not a full 15-inch (66.5 Wh), which is tighter than the 85-105% and 70-85% ChatGPT told the shopper. One caveat belongs on the page: Best Batteries reports the UGREEN's 100 W port falls to 45 W on laptops after 18-22 minutes, so 100 W is a peak figure.
candidates: Baseus EnerFill FC41 Digital Display Power Bank 20000mAh 100W

findings.label: MacBook Air fast-charge threshold (Apple)
findings.value: 70 W or higher USB PD source; up to 50% in around 30 minutes
findings.note: Page covers the M5 Air, both sizes: "Fast-charge capable with 70W or higher USB PD power source." The included adapter is a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max, so the in-box charger does not fast-charge either.

findings.label: Which MacBook Air models fast-charge and with which adapters (Apple support)
findings.value: MacBook Air introduced in 2022 or later; 140 W, 96 W or 70 W USB-C adapter; 67 W for the 13.6-inch only
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: Page dated November 05, 2026. A 65 W port sits below every adapter Apple lists, so it cannot fast-charge an Air.

findings.label: MacBook Air battery size (Apple)
findings.note: This is the denominator for every "how many charges" figure below.

findings.label: Headline 130 W normalised to per-port output
findings.value: USB-C1 alone 100 W; C1 + C2 = 100 + 30 = 130 W; C1 + USB-A = 122.5 W; all three = 115 W (C1 100 W, C2 and USB-A share 15 W)
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: Best Batteries reproduces the manual's table and says the allocation is fixed. Macworld gives the same split. The laptop port stays at 100 W in every combination, so 130 W is never a laptop charging speed.

findings.label: Same split, second source
findings.value: "The maximum charging power with two connected devices is 130W"; with three devices USB-C2 and USB-A are throttled to a shared 15 W
findings.source_title: Nexode Power Bank 20000mAh (130W) review: Compact, lightweight MacBook battery pack | Macworld
findings.note: Macworld also measured a MacBook Air M3 gaining 56% in 30 minutes on USB-C1, in line with Apple's "up to 50 percent in around 30 minutes".

findings.product: Baseus EnerFill FC41 Digital Display Power Bank 20000mAh 100W
findings.label: Headline 100 W normalised to shared output
findings.value: Each built-in USB-C cable and the USB-C port up to 100 W alone; with several outputs in use, one USB-C cable up to 65 W and the other three outputs share 15 W
findings.source_title: Baseus releases new 20K power bank with display in US - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Notebookcheck news article by Polly Allcock (13 Nov 2025, updated 17 Feb 2026) reporting Baseus's spec; it is not a measurement. 65 W is under Apple's 70 W line, so the Air loses fast charge once a phone is attached. baseus.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so this was not checked against the maker page.

findings.product: Baseus EnerFill FC41 Digital Display Power Bank 20000mAh 100W
findings.label: Recharge input, weight, size
findings.value: 65 W USB-C input, about 2 hours to full; 15.1 oz (about 428 g); 2.56 x 5.98 x 1.02 in
findings.source_title: Baseus releases new 20K power bank with display in US - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Figures as reported by Notebookcheck. It is the lightest of the four banks with a weight figure here (UGREEN 476 g, Anker 510 g, Cuktech 590 g).

findings.label: 20,000 mAh normalised to the maker's rated output
findings.value: 20,000 mAh is 4 x 5,000 mAh cells at 3.6 V (72 Wh); UGREEN rates 11,000 mAh at 5 V (55 Wh) and 3,000 mAh at 20 V (60 Wh)
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: Arithmetic: 60 Wh / 53.8 Wh = 1.12 of a 13-inch Air; 60 / 66.5 = 0.90 of a 15-inch, before the Mac's own charging loss. MacSources' spec table ("11000mAh rated capacity", "72Wh rated energy") and Parka Blogs ("11000 mAh rated capacity") give the same 5 V figure.

findings.label: Delivered energy by load (Best Batteries)
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: Best Batteries' figures, 76-90% of 72 Wh. Pulling the full 100 W costs about 3 Wh against a 60 W draw. 54.8 Wh / 53.8 Wh = 1.02 of a 13-inch Air; 54.8 / 66.5 = 0.82 of a 15-inch. This is already in a result ChatGPT got.

findings.label: 100 W as peak versus sustained (Best Batteries)
findings.value: The 100 W port falls to 65 W on a constant load, or 45 W on laptops, after 18 to 22 minutes
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: Best Batteries' statement, already in a result ChatGPT got. MacSources logged 84.4 W at the start of a 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro charge and 40.2-44.2 W with the bank at 9% and 3% (https://macsources.com/ugreen-130w-nexode-20000-power-bank-2024-review/, read 2026-11-26).

findings.label: Recharge input: maker rating versus Macworld
findings.value: 65 W max (20 V/3.25 A) on USB-C1 only per the spec table; Macworld wrote "up to 100W" and measured no more than 70 W
findings.source_title: UGREEN 130W Nexode 20000 Power Bank 2024 REVIEW - MacSources
findings.note: MacSources' spec table: USB-C1 input "65W Max". Best Batteries says the same and that UGREEN quotes about 2 hours with a 65 W PD charger. Use 65 W. The Costco built-in-cable variant ChatGPT described with "80W input" is a different model and was not read.

findings.label: Weight, size, cycle life
findings.value: 476 g (1.05 lb); 131 x 54 x 50.8 mm; Macworld says the 21700 cells should keep 80% capacity after 1,000 full cycles
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: Weight and size from Best Batteries; Parka Blogs and MacSources also give 476 g. Macworld weighed 480 g. The cycle-life figure is from the Macworld review, read 2026-11-26.

findings.label: Headline 220 W and "20K" normalised (Anker US page)
findings.value: USB-C 140 W max per port, USB-A 22.5 W, 220 W total; 20,100 mAh total capacity, "about 11,250 mAh to your devices"; input 100 W max; 1.12 lb (510 g)
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Power Bank (20K, 220W) - Anker US
findings.note: Anker's FAQ gives no voltage for the 11,250 mAh; at 5 V it would be 56.25 Wh (my arithmetic, assumption stated). Anker lists no Wh figure and no port-combination split on the page. An Air's fast-charge line is 70 W, so the 140 W port does nothing extra for it.

findings.label: Price at Anker US
findings.value: $119.99, list $179.99, in stock, delivery in 3-7 business days
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Power Bank (20K, 220W) - Anker US
findings.note: No pre-order notice. No sale end date was shown in what I read.

findings.label: Headline 165 W and 20,000 mAh normalised (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 20,000 mAh / 72 Wh (14.4 V x 5,000 mAh); rated 12,000 mAh at 5 V/3 A; USB-C ports up to 140 W and 65 W, USB-A 18 W; 165 W combined maximum, "a good 160 W" measured; input up to 165 W across both USB-C ports; 590 g
findings.source_title: The beast among the 20k power banks - Cuktech 15 Ultra review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: It is 20,000 mAh, not 25,000. 12,000 mAh x 5 V = 60 Wh (my arithmetic). Notebookcheck put about 53 Wh into a 13-inch iPad Pro with about 15% left in the bank, and measured 0-100% in 44 min 30 s in dual-port Beast Mode. Review published 2026-05-19, updated 2026-10-05.

findings.label: Three makers' usable-capacity ratings for "20K" banks, same basis
findings.value: UGREEN 130W: 55 Wh at 5 V, 60 Wh at 20 V; Anker Prime 20K: about 11,250 mAh (56.25 Wh if at 5 V); Cuktech 15 Ultra: 12,000 mAh at 5 V/3 A (60 Wh)
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: The table footnote: every bank's 20,000 mAh is counted at the 3.6 V cell (72 Wh), and the makers' own output ratings are 55-60 Wh. That is about one 13-inch Air (53.8 Wh) and 83-90% of a 15-inch (66.5 Wh), before the Mac's charging loss. Anker and Cuktech figures come from the anker.com and Notebookcheck pages cited above.
